questions.q: Why did David and Alan have to think first of all about speed when they set out?
choices: Their money was running very low
The soldiers had found the Maclarens' house
Winter snow would soon close the passes
Mr. Rankeillor was about to leave Scotland
questions.evidence: Our money was now run to so low an ebb that we must think first of all on speed

questions.q: Why did Alan want to cross by the old Bridge of Stirling instead of going round the head of the Forth?
choices: It was the last place soldiers would expect them
It was the shortest road and the soldiers had all gone home
A friend of Duncan's kept the bridge and would let them by
The fords at the head of the river were too deep after rain
questions.evidence: to go where ye are least expected

questions.q: Where did they hide during the day before trying the bridge?
choices: On a little sandy islet in Allan Water
In a ruined tower beside Stirling Castle
In a barn belonging to the shearers
Under the arches of the bridge itself
questions.evidence: we found a little sandy islet

questions.q: When they reached the quiet bridge, how did David and Alan differ?
choices: David wanted to push straight over; Alan wanted to wait and make sure
Alan wanted to swim the river, and David wanted to go looking for a boat
David wanted to turn back; Alan wanted to fight the sentry
Both were afraid and wanted to wait until morning came
questions.evidence: I was for pushing straight across; but Alan was more wary

questions.q: What happened as the old woman with the crutch stick went over the bridge?
choices: A sentry woke up and called out "Who goes?"
She fell and David ran out to help her up
She saw them behind the dyke and screamed
A party of dragoons rode across behind her

questions.q: Alan says the old woman's "foot still sounds boss upon the bridge." What does "boss" mean?
choices: Hollow
Quiet
Heavy
Quick

questions.q: How did David feel as they crawled away from the bridge?
choices: Bitterly disappointed to be back on the wrong side of Forth
Relieved that the sentry had not fired his musket at them
Proud that Alan had trusted him to keep watch so well
Excited because he was sure Alan had a clever plan
questions.evidence: I was so sharply cut by the disappointment

questions.q: Why did Alan say swimming the river was no answer?
choices: He could not swim
The current was too strong
The water was too cold
Soldiers watched the banks

questions.q: What could David see from Limekilns that made the place a heart-break for him?
choices: Queensferry across the water, where Mr. Rankeillor lived
Stirling Castle on its hill, with the red-coat drums beating
The House of Shaws standing on its lonely hill
The brig Covenant lying at anchor in the Hope
questions.evidence: looks across the Hope to the town of the Queensferry

questions.q: How much money did David have left by the time they reached Limekilns?
choices: Three silver shillings
Five pounds in a green purse
A single golden guinea piece
Nothing but a copper penny
questions.evidence: three silver shillings left to me of all my fortune

questions.q: Why did Alan say he wanted the lass at the change-house to feel sorry for David, not to fall in love with him?
choices: Pity would make her want to help them get hold of a boat
He wanted her to fall in love with Alan himself instead
He was afraid she would tell her father about David
He thought David was too young to be thinking of a lass
questions.evidence: I want her to be sorry for ye, David

questions.q: How did Alan act when they went back into the change-house?
choices: He half carried David and fed him like a sick child
He bragged loudly about his battles with the soldiers
He offered the maid his silver button for a boat
He sat apart and pretended not to know David
questions.evidence: he seemed to be half carrying me

questions.q: What was Alan hinting when he whistled "Charlie is my darling" and tapped the back of his neck?
choices: That David was a Jacobite who could lose his head for it
That David had a sore neck from sleeping in heather
That he wanted the maid to sing along with the tune
That soldiers were waiting outside the change-house
questions.evidence: meaning that I was old enough to lose my head

questions.q: Why was David unhappy with the part he played at the change-house?
choices: He hated to take part in lies
He was too hungry to listen
He wanted to pay for the food
He was afraid of the maid's father
questions.evidence: I ever hated to take part in lies

questions.q: What did David tell the lass that finally made her face clear up and agree to help?
choices: That he was going to Mr. Rankeillor and was loyal to King George
That he would pay her well once he had claimed his inheritance
That Alan was a famous soldier who had fought for Prince Charlie
That he had a rich uncle waiting for him at the House of Shaws
questions.evidence: King George has no truer friend in all Scotland than myself

questions.q: Who troubled them while they hid in the little wood by the sea?
choices: A drunken strolling piper
A party of red-coat soldiers
The maid's angry father
Two fishermen mending nets
questions.evidence: a strolling piper came and sat in the same wood with us

questions.q: How did the lass get them across the water?
choices: She stole a neighbour's boat and rowed them over herself
She paid an old fisherman to take them over the firth before dawn
She took them to the ferry and spoke to the boatman
She lent them her father's boat and they rowed alone
questions.evidence: stolen a neighbour's boat, and come to our assistance single-handed

questions.q: Afterward, why did David feel remorse as well as gratitude toward the lass?
choices: They had traded on her simple trust, and she might be in danger
She had refused to take any of their last three shillings
He had forgotten to ask her name before she rowed away
Alan had kept talking about her all night instead of sleeping
questions.evidence: remorse because we had traded upon her ignorance

questions.q: What is this chapter mostly about?
choices: Blocked at Stirling, they win a kind girl's help to cross the Forth
Alan builds a raft out of driftwood to float the two of them over the firth
The two are caught at the bridge and escape from Stirling Castle
David swims the Forth alone while Alan stays behind in the hills
questions.evidence: she had set us on the Lothian shore
